clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote to her sister Edna every day, Walter stayed out in the trees from dark to dark and grew distant from June, Glen got into fights at his new school, Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter and June fought over money for new trees, and by September June had joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out. The shifts show a family unsettled by the move and the distance from kin, with tension between Walter and June over the orchard work and money, and some settling as June found her place in the new community.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the frost took the crop and the bank called the loan: Walter drank heavily most nights, he and Glen blamed each other for the loan, Glen took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, you began wetting the bed in April 1969, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found around the same time, and by October Walter had stopped drinking and taken work pruning other men's trees. The shifts moved through the household as the loss of the orchard and its sale unsettled the family and pulled Glen into managing what his parents could not.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen sat out of work in the truck in the yard for hours, he and Marian fought loud fights at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother, and by June 1976 you were eating again and had made the track team. The shifts show Glen's loss of work stirring conflict between your parents, pulling Marian into overfunctioning, and drawing you into your own trouble as the household's balance shifted.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990, within the year: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows while Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice, Wilma took over Lily's care, you broke out in eczema on both hands, you and Hollis fought most nights, your mother drove over twice a week to take your side, Wilma moved to a flat in town in June 1991, and by August your eczema had cleared. The shifts show a household thrown into conflict by Wilma's arrival, with you caught between her and Hollis, the children unsettled, and your body holding the stress until the household could resettle after she left.
